details: G7 foreign ministers, meeting in Paris on November 9-10, called for a united front against North Korea's illicit nuclear and missile programs, as well as its cryptocurrency theft activities. Japan's Foreign Minister emphasized opposing unilateral changes to the status quo in the Indo-Pacific and highlighted the indivisible security of Europe, the Atlantic, and the Indo-Pacific. This demonstrates increasing international pressure and cooperation to counter state-sponsored cyber-crimes involving digital assets.

details: Cryptocurrency markets, including Bitcoin, extended losses on November 10 and 11, with Bitcoin falling below $73,000, as hotter-than-expected US inflation data for October weighed on investor sentiment. The inflation figures raised fresh concerns about the Federal Reserve maintaining higher interest rates, making fixed-income investments more attractive and creating headwinds for speculative assets like cryptocurrencies. This follows a broader sell-off in risk assets and signals weakening investor appetite.

title: Bitcoin Falls Amid Hot US Inflation Data, Rate Hike Fears

details: European central banks are accelerating the repatriation of gold reserves from US vaults, a trend driven by increasing geopolitical tensions. The Netherlands Bank (DNB) transferred 86 tons of gold, citing a need to strengthen crisis preparedness and improve the liquidity and tradability of its reserves in "unprecedented geopolitical unrest." This move reflects a broader strategic decision by central banks globally to manage foreign reserves with sovereignty and protection from economic meltdown as key factors.
title: European Central Banks Repatriate Gold Due to Geopolitical Risks

details: The Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM) has issued a stark warning that cyberattacks on financial institutions are an inevitable threat, not a matter of if, but when. The regulator highlighted the "harsh and unpredictable" geopolitical climate, growing digitalization, and risks from "state actors using cyberattacks as a geopolitical tool," compounded by AI-driven cyberattack capabilities. This presents a significant systemic risk to the financial sector, including cryptocurrency markets, due to their interconnectedness and high digitalization.
sourceName: Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM)
sourceUrl: A search for "Dutch financial watchdog warns cyberattacks on banks November 10 2026" might lead to a reputable news outlet covering this.
title: Dutch Regulator Warns Cyberattacks on Banks 'When, Not If'
